identification: Unmarked wooden wedge-arm (sliding-arm) plough plane, beech or boxwood-style, brass-tipped arms and brass thumb screw, five irons bundled with a rubber band. White '1855' is probably an inventory number. No maker stamp visible, so likely a common English or colonial made plane, not a named maker.

WebSearch was refused (turn budget used up) so no web searches were done: no resale price found at competitive houses, dealers or eBay. eBay sold listings for 'wooden plough plane complete with irons' and 'sash/plough plane brass arms' would settle it. chrome_hint: eBay AU and eBay.com sold items: 'wooden plough plane irons' and 'beech plough plane brass tip' (filter Sold Items); also Invaluable/LiveAuctioneers 'plough plane' completed lots
viewing_check: Look at the toe, heel and both sides for a maker stamp (e.g. Marples, Mathieson, Preston, Moseley, a colonial maker or a Sheffield tool-seller) and a brass-tipped arm quality; check that the irons number five and fit the slot, the wedge is present, the fence is not cracked or split, and whether the boxwood or ebony wear strips are present. A named maker would raise value.
